newsitem.title: CONGO: New Zaire talks planned, rebels to fight on.
newsitem.headline: New Zaire talks planned, rebels to fight on.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila failed on Sunday to agree terms of Mobutu's departure but fresh talks were planned in up to 10 days, mediators said.
But Kabila told Reuters by telephone from the South African ship where the talks took place that his rebels would fight on while Mobutu considered their demand that he resign.
U.N. and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, reading a final communique, told a closing news conference that Mobutu had offered to hand over to an elected president.
Kabila, for his part, insisted that his rebel alliance should act as the transitional authority to organise elections, the communique said.
South African President Nelson Mandela told the news conference on the customised icebreaker SAS Outeniqua that the fresh round of talks would be to "narrow the gap between the two parties".

Mandela, who hosted Sunday's meeting which lasted nearly an hour and a half, said Kabila had issued orders to his forces to stop advancing ahead of the talks but that this did not constitute a ceasefire.
"The question of a ceasefire is not part of his (Kabila's) vocabulary. What he is concerned with is that negotiations will lead to the end of hostilities," he added.
Witnesses said Mobutu left the ship immediately after the closing news conference. Kabila aides said the rebel leader planned to return to Angola.
Kabila told Reuters that his forces, who took up arms in October and control three quarters of the sprawling nation at the heart of Africa, would fight on.

"Mobutu has asked me to give him eight days while he considers our demand to resign. I have agreed to that request and we shall meet again on this same ship within the next eight days. But I have told him and the mediators that there will be no ceasefire while he considers our demands," he said.
